lesson.title: Reading Compounds in the Wild
lesson.subtitle: Split six-word monsters into meaning — Donaudampfschifffahrt territory

hook.title: The Monster Reading Method
hook.content: German compound monsters are famous: Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaft ('Danube steam-shipping company'). They terrify because learners read them as units. Read them as RUSSIANS? no — as stacks: split from the RIGHT, one head at a time. Gesellschaft (company) ← Schifffahrt (shipping) ← Dampf (steam) ← Donau (Danube). Each split gives a smaller compound; the RIGHTMOST word is always the head. Six splits and the monster is a sentence fragment: 'the Danube steam-shipping company'. You own every skill: head-word grammar from topic 21, compound reading, and the vocab pieces.

footnotes.title: Right-Headed, Always
footnotes.content: German compounds are right-headed: the LAST word is the grammatical head (gender, plural) and the semantic core. English compounds too ('school bus driver' — a driver, not a bus!). The right-split rule works because the head is always at the door.

pattern.title: Split, Head, Translate
pattern.content: Monster one: Donaudampfschifffahrt → Donau + Dampf + Schifffahrt = 'Danube-steam-shipping' — steam-boats on the Danube. Monster two: Unabhängigkeitserklärung → Unabhängigkeit (independence) + Erklärung (explanation/declaration) = 'declaration of independence' — and Erklärung is YOUR er- factory verb as a noun! Monster three: Zeitverschiebung → Zeit + Verschiebung (shift) = 'time-shift' — jetlag, via the -ung factory. Monster four: Krankenhaus? small now — Krankenhausfiliale? no — try: Handschuhfabrik → glove-factory. The method: right-split, read the head, stack the modifiers, translate bottom-up.
pattern.linguist_note: The famous longest words are legal texts: Rindfleischetikettierungsüberwachungsaufgabenübertragungsgesetz (the beef-labeling law of Mecklenburg, retired 2013). Every link was real grammar — Germans laugh at these too.

exercises.prompt: Split 'Zeitverschiebung' (jetlag): what is the HEAD word?
exercises.explanation: Right-split: the last word carries gender and meaning-core. die Verschiebung — the -ung factory again! Flugzeug splits the same way: Flug (flight) + Zeug (stuff) — the fly-stuff, neuter by the -zeug law.

exercises.prompt: Monster check: 'Donaudampfschifffahrt' — split from the right: what comes FIRST (leftmost)?
exercises.explanation: Modifiers stack leftward: Danube → steam → shipping. The leftmost piece is the outermost modifier.

exercises.prompt: Which monster contains YOUR er- factory noun?
exercises.explanation: die Erklärung is erklären's -ung... no, its own nominalization — 'the explanation'. The factory you drilled, fossilized into a monster.

exercises.prompt: 'Donaudampfschifffahrt' — which piece is a shift-family word you drilled (steam)?
exercises.explanation: Dampf/damp: the double-shift word from the Double-Shift Detectives — steaming inside the monster. The gallery walls hold more: Fußball, Regenbogen, Heimweh — and die Briefmarke, the stamp: Brief (letter) + Marke (mark), the little mark for the letter.

exercises.prompt: Assemble a mini-monster: 'The journey with the train is good'
exercises.target_answer: Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut
exercises.meaning: Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut
exercises.explanation: Two fahren-family nouns + mit + dative — the simple sentence that monsters are built from. And when the day comes: wir feiern den Geburtstag — the party verb takes the accusative present.

summary.outcome: Split wild compound monsters by right-heads and translate bottom-up.

use_example.german: Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut.
use_example.english: The journey by train is good.

summary.takeaway: Right-split every monster: the last word is the head, modifiers stack leftward — monsters are just long sentences.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: gender heuristics & suffix clues — decode der/die/das from the word's tail: -ung is feminine, -chen is neuter.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from Reading Compounds in the Wild (Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut):
twist.target_answer: Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Die Fahrt mit dem Zug ist gut" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of Reading Compounds in the Wild without relying on short-term echo.

zug.etymology_derivation: Noun of ziehen (to pull — the tow/tug family): a train is 'the pull(er)', an elevator the Aufzug ('up-pull'). [wiktionary]

fahrt.etymology_derivation: Noun of fahren (fare): a 'faring' — a drive, ride, or voyage; the -t is the Germanic -þ nominal suffix. [wiktionary]

dampf.context_phrase: Aus dem Topf steigt Dampf auf.
dampf.context_translation: Steam rises out of the pot.

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

zeit.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (cognate with English "tide", as in Yuletide or time and tide).

wort.etymology_derivation: Final d → t. Plural: Wörter / Worte.

kind.context_translation: The child plays in the garden.
kind.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kindą, related to the root of English kin — 'of the family'. The t → z shift never fired here; the d hardened to t instead. [wiktionary]

flugzeug.etymology_derivation: Flug (flight, from fliegen — English fly) + Zeug (gear, as in Feuerzeug): the fly-gear. [wiktionary]

briefmarke.etymology_derivation: Brief (the twin of brief, both from Latin brevis, short) + Marke (the twin of mark, both from Germanic mark-, sign) — a letter-mark, that is, a postage stamp. [wiktionary]

fußball.etymology_derivation: Fuß + Ball — a calque of English football; Fuß is foot with the t→s shift. [wiktionary]

regenbogen.context_phrase: Nach dem Regen sehen wir einen Regenbogen.
regenbogen.context_translation: After the rain we see a rainbow.
regenbogen.etymology_derivation: Regen (rain) plus Bogen (bow — twin of English bow); the page lists English rainbow as the parallel cognate — the exact same compound. [wiktionary]

heimweh.context_phrase: Nach einer Woche hatte sie Heimweh.
heimweh.context_translation: After a week she was homesick.
heimweh.etymology_derivation: Heim (home, Proto-Germanic *haimaz) + Weh (pain, from the root behind English woe): home-woe, homesickness. [wiktionary]

geburtstag.etymology_derivation: Geburt + Tag, exactly English birthday; the Tag/day pair shows the d to t stop shift, and Geburt comes from the gebären family. [wiktionary]

feiern.context_translation: We are celebrating a birthday today.
feiern.etymology_derivation: From Old High German firOn, from fira, from Latin feriae (festival days) - the same Latin word that became the English fair, a market held on feast days. [wiktionary][etymonline]

vanille.context_translation: The ice cream tastes of vanilla.
vanille.etymology_derivation: Borrowed around 1700 from French vanille, from Spanish vainilla; English vanilla comes from the same Spanish word. [wiktionary]
